title: What are the areas of these four parallelograms?
description: Four parallelograms are given by a base and the height drawn to it. The board multiplies each base by its height, and checks the last two with a rough estimate.
teaching_notes: One idea: area of a parallelogram is base times the height drawn to that base. Watch for students who use the slanting side in place of the height.

video_script.why: The child applies area as base times height from the solved examples to four parallelograms, including one where the height is longer than the base.
video_script.substitution: Multiply each base by the height drawn to it.
video_script.anchor: the book's four parallelograms, each with a base and a height marked
video_script.payoff_line: The areas are twenty eight, fifteen, twenty four and eight point eight square centimetres

final_answer.spoken: twenty eight, fifteen, twenty four and eight point eight square centimetres

maths_rules: (iii) the height 4.8 is drawn to the side 5: 5 × 4.8 = 24 cm²
(iv) the height 4.4 is drawn to the side 2: 2 × 4.4 = 8.8 cm²
video_script.design: Four parallelograms in a row, one step each. A rough estimate checks the last two.
open_questions: Parts (iii) and (iv) give a side with the height drawn to it; the figure is not in the extracted text, so the video takes that side as the base.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the area of each parallelogram?

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>The area of a parallelogram is its base times its height.
<bookmark mark='right'/>The height meets the base at a right angle.
<bookmark mark='any'/>Any side can be the base, if we take the height drawn to that side.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the area of each one.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: (i) base 7, height 4. Area = base × height = 7 × 4 = 28

marks.set: the first parallelogram is outlined with its base 7 and height 4

narration: <bookmark mark='set'/>Step one, for the first, the base is seven and the height is four.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Seven times four is twenty eight square centimetres.

marks.set: the second parallelogram is outlined with its base 5 and height 3

narration: <bookmark mark='set'/>Step two, for the second, the base is five and the height is three.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Five times three is fifteen square centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: (iii) the height 4.8 is drawn to the side 5, so that side is the base. Area = 5 × 4.8 = 24

marks.set: the side 5 lights up as the base with the height 4.8 beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='set'/>Step three, the height of four point eight is drawn to the side of five.
That side of five is the base.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Five times four point eight is twenty four square centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: (iv) the height 4.4 is drawn to the side 2, so that side is the base. Area = 2 × 4.4 = 8.8

marks.set: the side 2 lights up as the base with the height 4.4 beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='set'/>Step four, the height of four point four is drawn to the side of two.
<bookmark mark='base'/>The side of two is the base, even though the height is longer than it.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Two times four point four is eight point eight square centimetres.

beats.on_screen: check: 5 × 5 = 25, so 24 is a little less; 2 × 4 = 8, so 8.8 is a little more
narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step five, check the last two with a rough estimate.
For the third, five times five is twenty five. Four point eight is a little less than five.
<bookmark mark='chk2'/>For the fourth, two times four is eight. Four point four is a little more than four.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The areas are twenty eight, fifteen, twenty four and eight point eight square centimetres.
